chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj from some of our companions from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said:

The thief is not amputated until he confesses to the theft twice; if he returns [to confessing], he guarantees the theft, and he is not amputated if there are no witnesses. And he said: The fornicator is not stoned until he confesses four times; if there are no witnesses, and if he returns [to confessing], he is left alone and is not stoned.
ai.seo_question: What are the confession requirements for amputation of a thief and stoning of a fornicator in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Istibsar* highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of *al-istishab* (presumption of continuity) and the preference for withholding *hudud* in cases of doubt (*shubuhat*). It specifies that for theft, two confessions suffice for amputation while guaranteeing restitution, whereas fornication requires four confessions for stoning if no witnesses are present, reflecting the rigorous evidentiary standards derived from the Imams.
